headline: UK to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements
summary: British Foreign Secretary David Lammy (referred to as Edward Miliband in the source) may formally announce the ban on business investments in illegal settlements to align with ICJ rulings.
details: The United Kingdom is preparing to ban trade and business investments in illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories. British Foreign Secretary David Lammy (referred to as Edward Milband in the source) is expected to announce the formal ban soon.

The move follows a July 2024 International Court of Justice (ICJ) advisory opinion that declared Israel's occupation of Palestinian territories illegal and called on other nations to oppose settlement activity.

The proposed ban would prohibit British citizens and businesses from engaging in economic or financial activities that support the illegal settlements, aligning with the UK's commitment to international human rights law and the Geneva Conventions.
Israel has reacted strongly to the potential ban, with Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar warning that Israel would take countermeasures if the UK acts against it.

The tension has extended beyond the trade ban, with reports that Donald Trump has suggested he may reconsider the US position on the Falkland Islands' sovereignty, potentially using it as leverage in diplomatic negotiations.

British Foreign Secretary David Lammy (referred to as Edward Milband in the source) recently described the situation in Gaza as 'horrific' after meeting with aid workers, emphasizing the need for the UK government to act more decisively.

headline_marked: Tk 601.79 crore [[Khulna City Corporation announces budget]] for current fiscal year
headline: Tk 601.79 crore Khulna City Corporation announces budget for current fiscal year
summary: The proposed budget focuses on waste management, mosquito control, and permanently solving the city's long-standing waterlogging issues.
details: Khulna City Corporation (KCC) has officially announced a proposed budget of Tk 601.79 crore for the current fiscal year, as presented by Administrator Nazrul Islam Manju.
The budget estimates revenue income of Tk 211.90 crore, while overall operating expenses are projected at Tk 241.44 crore.
The city corporation expects to receive a general grant of Tk 197.62 crore from the government, along with an additional Tk 79.46 crore for special development projects.
Administrator Nazrul Islam Manju assured residents that no new taxes have been imposed on the public in this budget.
The budget places maximum emphasis on improving the quality of life and ensuring citizen services through enhanced waste management and mosquito eradication programs.

Special allocations have been made to permanently resolve waterlogging, a primary concern for Khulna residents, by prioritizing the modernization and expansion of the drainage system and repairing internal city roads.
caption:
Tk 601.79 crore for city development! No new taxes for Khulna residents in the latest budget announcement.

Khulna City Corporation (KCC) has officially announced a proposed budget of Tk 601.79 crore for the current fiscal year, as presented by Administrator Nazrul Islam Manju.

The budget estimates revenue income of Tk 211.90 crore, while overall operating expenses are projected at Tk 241.44 crore.

The city corporation expects to receive a general grant of Tk 197.62 crore from the government, along with an additional Tk 79.46 crore for special development projects.

Administrator Nazrul Islam Manju assured residents that no new taxes have been imposed on the public in this budget.

The budget places maximum emphasis on improving the quality of life and ensuring citizen services through enhanced waste management and mosquito eradication programs.

Special allocations have been made to permanently resolve waterlogging, a primary concern for Khulna residents, by prioritizing the modernization and expansion of the drainage system and repairing internal city roads.
